text:
maria: Hey team — running a POC for Acme, hitting 403 on every call. Customer says they copied the API key from the dashboard. sample curl in logs: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hi"}'
```
Response: `{"error":{"message":"permission denied: org mismatch","code":403}}`
Anyone seen this exact msg? Need a quick checklist before I hop on call. :alarm_clock:

alex: yep, that wording usually means the key is bound to a different org/tenant than the `Redwood-Org` header or the project in the request. quick checklist: key validity, org header, token binding, scope.

presales-bot: FYI — POC trial keys are often scoped to a single org and 1 project by default. Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth#key-bindings :information_source:

kevin: @maria can you paste the exact request headers the customer is sending (sanitized)? also what type of key — service key vs project key?

maria: customer pasted this header dump: 
`Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123`
`Redwood-Org: acme-enterprise`
`X-Project: default`
They said the dashboard shows key bound to "acme-internal" though.

sam: ah — org mismatch confirmed. Two quick fixes: 1) ask them to use the org the key is bound to (acme-internal) in the `Redwood-Org` header, or 2) generate a new key scoped to acme-enterprise and share it. For demos we can also create a temporary unbound key if legal approves.

jen: to troubleshoot in the meantime you can decode the key's tenant claim locally: `echo "sk_live_ABC123" | base64 -d` won't work for opaque keys — instead ask us for the key id and we can look up binding server-side. If they can run `jwt decode` do that, otherwise send key id.

maria: running into resistance — they say rotating keys is blocked by security team. Any way to allow the existing key to work for the demo without rotation?

alex: you can add an override mapping on our side for POC accounts (requires approval). I'll open an internal ticket. If they just need read-only generation for 30 minutes, we can attach a temporary project to the key. @kevin can you approve?

kevin: give me the account id and key id. I'll fast-track an override for up to 1 hour. Please confirm this is only for the demo and we'll audit after.

maria: account id `acct_98765`, key id `key_4-demo`. Customer also asked if rate limits could be causing 403 — they saw 429 earlier. Thoughts?

sam: 429 = rate limit, 403 = auth. Separate issues. 429 for trial defaults to 10 RPS and 600 TPS tokenized; we can bump to 25 RPS for short demos. 403 is definitely the org binding.

presales-bot: Checklist: [x] confirm key id, [x] confirm org header, [ ] decide rotate vs override, [ ] temporary RPS bump if needed, [ ] audit log note.

maria: thanks — I'll tell the security team the path: temporary override + RPS bump for 1 hour. Also sharing a quick debug curl to test once they change header: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123" 
 -H "Redwood-Org: acme-internal" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"status"}'
```
If that returns 200 they're good. Will update once they confirm. :thumbsup:

jen: if it still 403 after header change collect server request-id (x-rw-request-id) and last 3 chars of the key id and DM me. I can trace it in audit logs.

maria: got it. pinging them now. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
